title: How WinterPath works
intro: What data we use, how we label it, what our model does and doesn't do, and how we treat your privacy.

sources.title: Sources and licences
sources.intro: This list comes from the API, which reports each source's licence and last successful refresh.
sources.name: Source

attribution.title: Map attribution
attribution.body: The planner map uses OpenFreeMap vector tiles built from OpenStreetMap. Attribution stays visible on the map at all times.

evidence.title: Evidence states
evidence.intro: Every condition, closure, report or estimate carries exactly one of these labels, always shown with an icon and text.

conditions.title: Winter conditions: what we can actually know
conditions.intro: Pick a condition to see which data source covers it, how WinterPath uses it and which evidence label it gets.
conditions.illustrative: Illustrative scene — not a real street or live conditions.
conditions.sceneDescription: Illustrative 3D scene of one block: a triplex with an exterior staircase, a sidewalk, a snowbank, a roadwork barrier, a 311 report marker and an icy patch. The selected condition is highlighted.

steps.label: Exterior stairs
steps.source: Stairs and steps on the walking network come from OpenStreetMap (highway=steps).
steps.use: The step-free profile uses only segments tagged as step-free in OpenStreetMap (community-mapped). Steps, and segments without such a tag, are left out rather than guessed.
steps.evidenceNote: Community-mapped tags, not a verified accessibility check. Segments without a tag are Unknown.

closure.label: Sidewalk work
closure.source: Ville de Montréal roadwork permits (Entraves et travaux en cours).
closure.use: A sidewalk is avoided only while the permit is active and its sidewalk_blockedtype field says pedestrian passage is blocked. When the permit is confirmed but whether work is active at your walking time is not, that is shown as Unknown. Roadwork alone never means a closed sidewalk.
closure.evidenceNote: The permit record is official data; it says nothing about snow or ice.

reports.label: 311 reports
reports.source: Ville de Montréal 311 requests (for example about snow or ice), grouped by area.
reports.use: Shown as reports from residents, never as confirmed obstacles.
reports.evidenceNote: A report is not a verified condition.

snowLoading.label: Snow removal
snowLoading.source: The city's street snow-loading schedules (Planif-Neige). Optional source; it needs a city access token.
snowLoading.use: A street loading schedule does not certify that a sidewalk has been cleared. WinterPath never uses it to describe a sidewalk as cleared.
snowLoading.evidenceNote: No sidewalk condition is derived from it.

weather.label: Ice and fresh snow
weather.source: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) weather observations.
weather.use: Weather describes the area, not a specific sidewalk. A risk layer (a validated model or a labelled heuristic) can turn it into a per-segment estimate; the model section shows which one is active and how it was evaluated. Without a risk layer, segment risk is Unknown, never low.
weather.evidenceNote: Only when a risk layer is on: a validated model or a labelled heuristic.

model.title: Model card
model.intro: Our optional risk layer predicts reporting activity, not ice. It is only switched on after it beats a simple baseline on held-out data.

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.schematic: Schematic of the pilot area (not to scale with streets).

privacy.title: Privacy (Québec Law 25)
points: No accounts and no route history. Route requests are processed in memory.
Your location is requested only when you press "Use my location", and only after we explain why.
Server logs keep only coarse location (about 100 m), never your precise coordinates.
Community reports store an exact location only with your explicit consent, expire after 72 hours, and can be deleted with your deletion code.
Pilot enquiries keep minimal contact details for 12 months.
privacy.review: This privacy approach has not yet been reviewed by legal counsel.

limitations.title: Limitations
points: We never describe a sidewalk as safe, cleared, ice-free or wheelchair accessible unless an official source verifies it.
311 requests are reports, not confirmed obstacles. Many conditions are never reported.
Snow-loading plans do not certify that a sidewalk has been cleared.
Roadwork does not mean the sidewalk is closed unless the permit data says so.
Coverage is limited to the pilot area; network gaps are reported, not guessed.
